# Results - Study 247 (Bond-Seasonality) on the real tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The turn-of-month (TOM)
window is defined as the last 2 and first 2 trading days of each calendar month, derived
purely from the trading index (no external calendar). We measure mean daily returns on TOM
vs all other days (HAC t-stats, Wilson win-rate intervals), run a **TOM-only** book
against buy-and-hold (net of 1 bp/leg), and separately test the turn-of-year (TOY, last
5 + first 5 trading days per year). As-of **2026-06-12**; match the fingerprints to
confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Adjustment | Window | Rows | TOM days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| TLT | **total-return** | 2002-07-30 -> 2026-06-12 | 6,007 | 1,150 | `f83a9db36f17` |
| IEF | **total-return** | 2002-07-30 -> 2026-06-12 | 6,007 | 1,150 | `a83262b21d6b` |

Both ETFs are **total-return adjusted** (dividends reinvested).

## The effect - TOM vs every other day

| Ticker | TOM mean | Other-day mean | Gap | HAC *t* (gap) | Win-rate TOM | Win-rate rest |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TLT** | **6.67 bps** | 0.71 bps | **+5.95 bps** | **+1.99** | 54.7% [51.8, 57.5] | 51.5% [50.1, 52.9] |
| **IEF** | **4.62 bps** | 0.76 bps | **+3.86 bps** | **+2.66** | 54.7% [51.9, 57.6] | 51.1% [49.7, 52.5] |

The TOM gap is present in both ETFs: bonds do earn more at the turn of the month than in
mid-month. However, the evidence is **mixed and soft**: the IEF (medium duration) gap
clears the *t* = 2 bar (+2.66), but TLT (long duration, the noisier instrument) is just
below (+1.99). The win-rate superiority is modest and the Wilson intervals barely
separate.

## Turn-of-year (TOY) - last 5 + first 5 trading days of each calendar year

| Ticker | TOY gap | HAC *t* (gap) | n_toy |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| TLT | -2.38 bps | -0.40 | 250 |
| IEF | +1.48 bps | +0.53 | 250 |

The turn-of-year effect in Treasuries is **absent**. Both t-stats are far below the bar,
and the signs are not even consistent. This is noise, not signal.

## Could you trade it? - a TOM-only book (net of 1 bp/leg)

| Arm | CAGR | Sharpe (whole tape) | Sharpe (per invested day) | Days invested | MaxDD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TLT TOM-only** | **2.81%** | 0.470 | 1.119 | 1,150 (19.1%) | -18.4% |
| TLT Buy & hold | 3.71% | 0.326 | - | 100% | - |
| **IEF TOM-only** | **1.96%** | 0.657 | 1.599 | 1,150 (19.1%) | -7.5% |
| IEF Buy & hold | 3.60% | 0.553 | - | 100% | - |

The TOM-only book is in the market 19% of the time. Unlike extreme calendar rules (e.g.
pre-holiday, ~4% invested), this is enough time to build a meaningful return - but it
still consistently **underperforms buy-and-hold** in CAGR. The Sharpe on the whole tape
is higher than buy-and-hold for IEF (0.66 vs 0.55) because the book avoids mid-month
volatility, but this is a risk-reduction story, not a return-enhancement story: the book
earns less in absolute terms.

## How to read it

- **Signal -> WEAK.** The TOM gap is positive and consistent across TLT and IEF. IEF
  clears the HAC *t* = 2 bar (+2.66) but TLT does not (+1.99). The turn-of-year effect
  is absent (both t-stats near zero). With ~23 years of data and a modest 3-4 bps gap,
  the evidence is suggestive but not robust across instruments: one clearing the bar and
  one not is the definition of Weak, not Real.
- **Tradability -> Mirage.** The TOM-only book underperforms buy-and-hold in CAGR on
  both instruments despite its higher whole-tape Sharpe (a risk-reduction artefact). A
  calendar-only book that captures the TOM window and sits in cash otherwise cannot
  compete with simply holding Treasuries, which already earn the term premium on every
  day.
- **Myth check - "bonds have a reliable calendar bid"**: MIXED. The month-end bid
  (institutional rebalancing into fixed income) is theoretically plausible and shows up
  in the data at a suggestive level, but it is too soft to call reliably confirmed.

python examples/verify.py
